subject: Strategic waiver rationale & risk mitigation — CuraLife pilot (VP/CFO review)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Strategic waiver rationale & risk mitigation — CuraLife pilot (VP/CFO review)

Team — sending a concise memo and ask: CuraLife (pilot for their clinical documentation workflow) is asking for a 45% first-year onboarding discount, plus a waived VPC setup fee, to accelerate the close this quarter. Net ARR is relatively small for year 1 (~$180k run-rate) but they’re positioned to expand quickly into three more lines-of-business in 2027 given the roadmap discussion last week.

Why I’m escalating: this request is outside our standard commercial guardrails (both % and waiver of one-time fees). Sales believes the incremental upside (channel references + potential cross-sell) justifies consideration, but we need explicit VP/CFO authorization and a clear mitigation plan.

Attached: short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) with clear milestones, and a draft contract amendment (redlines in the docx). Ask for review: 1) decision on discount % / term (approved, counter, or deny) 2) whether we can waive the VPC fee under a conditional clause 3) required safeguards (payment terms, milestone-based release of credits, or escrow).

Quick summary bullets: 
- Proposed commercial: 45% off first-year usage + waive $25k VPC setup fee.
- Customer ask tied to immediate go-live by Nov 1 and reseller commitment.
- Risk: sets a precedent for prescriptive waivers; financial impact minor now but scales if replicated.

Next step: Markus/Kimberly — can you please flag whether this is approvable as-is, or list required mitigations? Jordan — if you can add one-sentence commercial fallback (e.g., 30% + $10k setup credit) that helps.

Thanks,
Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: CuraLife_MutualActionPlan_v3.pdf (PDF, 2 pages), amendment-draft-CuraLife.docx (MS Word, redlines)

From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Strategic waiver rationale & risk mitigation — CuraLife pilot (VP/CFO review)

Marissa — thanks for the concise brief. A couple quick thoughts and data requests before I can sign off: 

1) Financial exposure: run the net present value for the first 24 months with the 45% applied (include token/embedding economics).
2) Precedent check: list any similar waivers in the last 12 months (customer & brief outcome).
3) Milestone triggers: I will consider a conditional waiver if credits are released against documented milestones (go-live, usage thresholds, payment on time). NO unconditional fee waivers.

Tentative response: conditional approval of a reduced structure: 35% first-year discount + $12.5k setup credit contingent on milestones and a 12-month minimum commitment. If Jordan can confirm the fallback revenue model, I’ll clear to Kimberly for final accounting treatment and revenue recognition implications.

Please get those numbers into the MAP and re-upload.

-Markus
VP Finance
Redwood Inference

Marissa / Jordan / Markus / Elena — reviewed the updated MAP and the revenue scenarios. My read and final ask: 

Decision: APPROVE conditional commercial as follows (for VP/CFO sign-off):
- 35% discount on year-1 usage (not tokens) with a hard cap on total discounted dollars equal to $85k.
- $12.5k setup credit (refundable) released in two tranches: 50% on go-live, 50% on 90 days sustained usage > agreed baseline.
- 12-month minimum committed ARR contract.
- All credits to be recognized as contra-revenue and only refundable if customer hits the milestones; include clawback language for early termination.

Required docs before sign-off: 
1) Jordan — finalize amendment with the milestone language and include a clause prohibiting replication of the same unconditional waiver for other new customers (to limit precedent).
2) Legal/Revenue Ops review for recognition & clawback language (I’ll route once Jordan uploads).
3) Marissa — get an explicit commitment date for go-live (Nov 1 target) and a named PoC who will validate milestone completion.

Elena — appreciate the urgency. If this structure is acceptable, we’ll move to a DocuSign packet and ask for countersignature this week. If you prefer a higher discount, our ask is an expanded 24-month committed ARR instead of 12.

Kimberly Park
VP, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference
